headline: Wichita County Home Backup Report
summary: Wichita County has a moderate outlook. It sees a long outage of 12 hours or more about once every 10 years. This comes from 8 years of records since 2018. In February 2021, 16% of homes in the county lost power. The longest-waiting tenth waited about 62 hours. In August 2023, 12% of homes in the county lost power. The longest-waiting tenth waited about 46 hours. One Core lasts about 18 hours in August. One Core lasts about 50 hours in November. Two Cores last about 37 hours in August. The suggested number of Cores is 2 Cores. This covers 98% of past 12-hour-plus outage hours. Base confirms sizing at install.
